subject: Helix Q4 renewal: usage reconciliation, perf regression note, and preflight PO
messages:
From: Tom Rivers <trivers@helixtx.com>
To: sean_gallagher@redwoodinference.com
Cc: Sofia Mendes <sofia.m@helixtx.com>, Helix Procurement <procurement@helixtx.com>
Date: Tue, 2 Nov 2027 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Helix Q4 renewal discussion

Hey Sean —

Thanks for the call earlier. Quick recap from our side: Q3 token consumption hit about 28M tokens (up 62% q/q) after we rolled the recommendation engine to 80% of traffic. We had two small latency blips during the higher tail (p95 went from 210ms to 360ms on a few POST bursts) that impacted the real-time scoring SLA for a handful of customers.

Before we sign anything long-form we need: (1) a short reconciliation of which routes/models drove that 62% increase, (2) a perf note with mitigation (was it batching policy? model change?), and (3) a clean preflight PO for internal approvals — procurement needs a single PDF they can attach to their finance entry.

Can you send the CSV export and the preflight PDF? If we can get that by EOD Wednesday we can route to Finance for a Nov 10 approval.

— Tom

Attachments: none (Tom referenced internal Helix logs)

From: sean_gallagher@redwoodinference.com
To: Tom Rivers <trivers@helixtx.com>
Cc: monica_patel@redwoodinference.com, laura_bennett@redwoodinference.com
Date: Tue, 2 Nov 2027 11:02:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Helix Q4 renewal discussion

Tom — thanks for the clear ask. Attaching a short reconciliation and our preflight PO template; see notes inline below.

Summary (high level):
- Q3 consumption: 28,042,937 total tokens (text-generation + embeddings). Model mix shifted 54% gpt-large-instruct / 46% opt-13b-equivalent after the recommender rollout.
- Primary driver: the recommender ensemble increased average prompt size (context + features) from ~420 tokens to ~760 tokens per request for scored sessions. That explains ~48% of the q/q delta.
- Secondary driver: a 12% increase in session volume due to onboarding two new enterprise accounts.
- Perf regression: p95 spikes were correlated with concurrent long-history queries + small batch sizes. We observed KV-cache warm-up penalties on cold-starts and a suboptimal batching window for traffic bursts.

Mitigation & ROI notes:
- Short-term: we recommend enabling 'adaptive batching' for the scoring route (reduces p95 in our tests by ~120ms) and enabling prefix cache for 10-minute hot keys. Operational change is low-friction and has no model change.
- Mid-term (if you go reserved): a modest commitment uplift from current run-rate to a 1.5x Q4 committed token block yields 18–25% unit cost savings across gen+embed mix (we ran the math in the attached CSV).
- Preflight PO: attached preflight_po_template.pdf — fill billing contact + PO number. If procurement signs that, we can lock pricing and schedule an ops preflight with our SREs.

Next steps I propose:
1) Helix signs preflight PO (procurement).
2) Redwood enables adaptive batching and prefix cache on the scoring route for a 72-hour canary.
3) Run a 7-day traffic replay post-canary and validate p95 and token delta (we'll provide a report).

I'll also loop Monica for contract language and Laura for billing/entitlement.

Best —
Sean Gallagher
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
sean_gallagher@redwoodinference.com
+1 (415) 555-0199

Attachments: usage_by_model_Q3.csv, preflight_po_template.pdf

Sean — appreciate the quick reconciliation. Two quick clarifying Qs from Procurement before we circulate to Finance:

1) On the proposed 1.5x commitment, can you provide the blended unit delta (per-1k-token) for both generation and embeddings separately? Our cost model splits those into different buckets.
2) The latency mitigation: will adaptive batching require SDK changes from our side or is it a server-side routing change? We need to confirm with the infra team.

If answers are quick we should be able to get a PO-ready PDF back to you by Thu 11/4 so Finance can meet the 11/10 deadline.

Thanks,
Sofia
Director, Platform Operations — Helix Therapeutics

Sofia / Tom — quick answers and operational commitments from our side.

1) Unit economics: generation = $0.82 per 1k tokens at current monthly run-rate; with a 1.5x committed block that drops to ~$0.66 per 1k (approx -19.5%). Embeddings (dense) move from $1.35 to $1.08 per 1k (approx -20%). Detailed line items are in usage_by_model_Q3.csv.

2) Adaptive batching: server-side change only — no SDK modifications required. We'll toggle a per-route flag in the Console and roll a canary. We'll provide the exact canary playbook (traffic slice, detection rules, rollback thresholds).

Operational ask: please confirm the PO billing contact and the legal entity name exactly as it should appear on the invoice. Once we have the preflight PO signed we will schedule the SRE-run canary (target start: Fri 11/5) and deliver a 7-day replay report by Tue 11/16.

Happy to hop on a 20-min call to walk procurement through the PO fields.

— Monica Patel
